scope: Read-only static sub-review of final selected width-eight P256 Montgomery field and affine coordinate hooks, thin Invert adapter, managed payload codec, and direct ODD_GENERATOR consumer. This is not full plugin/SDK approval.
conclusion: No current-source blocker found within this field-hook sub-review. The frozen width-eight table and direct odd-generator consumers preserve the unchecked field/affine restoration preconditions under the protected prepared-value contract. Final independent native tests, all-engine tests, GC tests, and SDK protection remain the parent audit responsibility.
invariants: FieldElement stores canonical residues a*2^256 mod p. Valid upstream input paths and add/sub/multiply/square/negate preserve the integer range [0,p). Existing field32.rs and field64.rs are unchanged.
On target_pointer_width=64, U256::to_words/from_words copy four integer limbs; no transmute, layout reinterpretation, unaligned access, or padding serialization is introduced.

The two Montgomery accessors are absent on 32-bit targets. Repository runtime builds explicitly target Wasm64 and owner scopes native tests to 64-bit. This is a supported-target limitation, not a silent 32-bit representation mismatch. The thin Invert adapter is width-independent.
Affine restore forces infinity=0 and is correct only for validated on-curve nonidentity points. It must never round-trip AffinePoint::IDENTITY using coordinates alone.

Preparation validates canonical compressed/uncompressed SEC1 through PublicKey::from_sec1_bytes. For the selected WIDTH=8 and ROWS=32, every table coefficient is c=sum(b_j*2^(32*j)), j=0..7, with at least one bit set. Thus 0<c<2^225<n. P256 has prime group order and cofactor one, so no nonidentity input key yields an identity table entry.

POINTS=255 and 64 bytes per point give a 16320-byte payload, matching compiler/prepared_layout.ml. compiler/key_type.ml registers owner p256 and P256PreparedPublicKey; register.ml wraps preparation and unwraps verification with this same token.
Payload encoding is eight explicit little-endian u64 integers per point, x then y. Decoding uses from_le_bytes on copied eight-byte slices, independent of payload alignment and host byte order.

ODD_GENERATOR is generated from G by repeated addition of 2G, yielding G,3G,...,15G. Its coordinate conversion uses coordinate*2^256 mod p, followed by four numeric low-to-high u64 limbs per coordinate, exactly as the prepared generator table. These constant points are nonidentity because 1<=2*i+1<=15<n.

Direct verification decodes immutable ODD_GENERATOR constants with point_from_words. The width-five NAF path emits signed odd digits of magnitude 1..15; magnitude/2 selects indices 0..7. Negative digits subtract the same restored point. All lookup choices depend only on public verification scalars.

Unchecked restore consumers are private point_from_words called from immutable GENERATOR/ODD_GENERATOR constants or the prepared payload path. Wasm export safety contract requires the exact current-build payload size and valid protected provenance.
Prepared payload trust depends on nominal SDK protection and immutability. The raw unsafe native export is not an arbitrary untrusted byte decoding API.

The elliptic_curve::ops::Invert implementation calls FieldElement::invert(self), which resolves to the inherent method rather than recursive trait dispatch. Inherent inversion returns CtOption::None for zero and unchanged exponentiation/arithmetic preserves canonical output residues.

Upstream BatchNormalize initializes every z workspace slot to ONE, copies a projective z only when nonzero, then batch-inverts the nonzero product. Original zero-z points are conditionally mapped back to affine identity. Direct BatchInvert on a zero-containing batch returns None.

Upstream batch inversion reports failure for empty input and normalization unwraps its result. The selected prepared table has a positive compile-time POINTS=255, so this inherited empty-input edge is unreachable through plugin preparation.
